Heard on I.A. No.16633/2025, which is first application under Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.) for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant - Bheemsingh S/o Puniya Dabur.

The appellant has been convicted for commission of offences punishable under Sections 363, 366A and 376(2)(N) of IPC alongwith Section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 01 year with fine of Rs.1,000/-, RI for 03 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- and life imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/-
respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the allegation against the appellant is of committing rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
Counsel for appellant argued that the prosecutrix was a consenting party, which is evident from her statement.

He argued that appellant has been convicted in the case on the basis of age of the prosecutrix, which has been proved by the prosecution on the basis of scholar register though, the 2 CRA-8784-2025 prosecution has not proved the source of recording the age of the prosecutrix in the scholar register.
He further argued that age of the appellant was also 20 years at the time of incident.
Appellant has already remained in jail for 02 years 03 months.
Final hearing of the appeal may take time hence, it is prayed that the appellant be granted bail.
Counsel for the State opposed the application however, counsel for the objector pleads no objection.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration all the facts in entirety,

sentences.text: 1 statement of the prosecutrix that she had gone with the appellant on two wheeler and stayed with him for 2-3 days, we find that the prosecutrix was a consenting party and prosecution has failed to establish the source of recording of her age in the scholar register.
Apart from that, the appellant was also 20 years of age at the time of incident and he has already remained in jail for 02 years 03 months.
Appeal is of the year 2025 and final hearing of the same may take time.

In the case of Tejubai Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75 , it has been held that if the date of birth of the prosecutrix in the school register is recorded on the basis of a person who made entry of the date of birth, the same is not sufficient to prove the age.

entities.text: Tejubai Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the same, we deem it appropriate to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.16633/2025 is allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant - Bheemsingh shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and he be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of 3 CRA-8784-2025 Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 21.07.2026 and all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
With the aforesaid, IA No.16633/2025 stands disposed of.
